+# The full finite named family
+
+## Abstract
+
+Finite canonical native branching before free-shape unification
+
+X is the entire declared finite family of names, represented by a presentation p. An Equation is a primitive definition z=T(n), a native shift definition z=rho to power a of x, an ordered pair definition z=pair(x,y), or an equality x=y. Every occurrence of a name refers to the same original source value. Unused declared names remain in X. Source consists of arbitrary finite ordered Boolean trees, and rho is the actual native substitution, not a free unary symbol. In the display, canonicalCodes(v)(x)=encode(v(x)), canonicalShapes(v)(x)=shape(encode(v(x))), NativeHolds is Equation.Holds, and BranchHolds is BranchEquation.Holds.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Executable finite constructor choices).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositiveBranchReduction.branches`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositiveBranchReduction.branches` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+choices retains primitive, shift and equality equations. For each pair definition it offers exactly an ordinary case and a collapse case. branches forms their finite ordered product over the whole input list, retaining repeated constraints. An ordinary case requires the output code to be the pair of its input codes. A collapse case requires input ranks r+1 and r and output rank r+2 for some unrestricted natural r. That rank is not enumerated or bounded. Every code in the theorem is the actual canonical encode of the same original valuation.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (Erase ranks only after selecting cases).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositiveBranchReduction.shape`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositiveBranchReduction.shape` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+shape replaces each primitive rank by one fixed free primitive leaf and preserves ordered pairs. Primitive definitions and collapse cases become primitive shape equalities. Shift definitions become equalities of shapes. An ordinary pair definition becomes a free binary constructor equation. No interpreted native power is sent to the free occurs check. The exact canonical branch equations are retained alongside these weaker free-shape equations.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (Retain the actual scalar and block offsets).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositiveBranchReduction.sourceOffsetEdges`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositiveBranchReduction.sourceOffsetEdges` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The source comparison carrier traverses the selected branch equations before rank erasure. A shift edge carries its actual natural offset as an integer; ordinary and equality comparisons carry zero. Primitive and collapse equations contribute no residual edge because their residual-free comparisons are against primitive leaves, while their original scalar and collapse constraints remain in BranchEquation.Holds. The edge carrier retains every occurrence and every repeated comparison.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (Project the source offset carrier to undirected adjacency).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositiveBranchReduction.sourceOccurrenceEdges`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositiveBranchReduction.sourceOccurrenceEdges` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Projecting an offset edge forgets only its numeric offset and keeps its two residual occurrences. The resulting list is the source graph adjacency generated by every ordinary, shift, equality, constant and collapse comparison. Collapse scalar equations are retained in the branch data even when their residual projection is empty.
+
+**Definition 1.5 (Connectivity of the actual source comparison graph).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositiveBranchReduction.sourceConnected`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositiveBranchReduction.sourceConnected` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+sourceConnected is the equivalence closure of sourceOccurrenceEdges. Its vertices are the same total occurrenceVertices supplied by the MGU action, including isolated occurrences of unused names. It is defined from the source branch constructors and only then related to the free-shape graph.
+
+**Theorem 1.6 (Exact source-to-shape graph identification).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositiveBranchReduction.source_comparison_graph_identification`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositiveBranchReduction.source_comparison_graph_identification` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every finite selected branch and every total term assignment, the projected source comparison carrier is definitionally traversed over the same named terms as the shape equations. The proof checks each primitive, shift, ordinary, collapse and equality constructor: shift retains its integer offset, ordinary and equality retain their corresponding leaves, and constant or collapse comparisons project to no residual edge. Therefore the source adjacency list is exactly occurrenceEdges(shapeEquations B, s), with no dropped or added occurrence.
+
+**Theorem 1.7 (Actual source connectivity has one component per residual sort).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositiveBranchReduction.source_connected_iff_sort`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositiveBranchReduction.source_connected_iff_sort` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For an actual successful free-shape MGU, sourceConnected on the source comparison carrier is equivalent, for all total vertices, to equality of residual sort. This is an exact application of the existing MGU occurrence theorem through the proved source graph identification; the source quantifiers retain every declared name, every occurrence and the original branch scalar/rank constraints.
+
+**Theorem 1.8 (Exact canonical branching with total MGU shape reconstruction).**
+
+$$\forall X: Type, (\forall p: \operatorname{Presentation}\left(X\right), (\forall E: \operatorname{List}\left(\operatorname{Equation}\left(X\right)\right), (\forall v: X \to Source, ((\forall e: \operatorname{Equation}\left(X\right), ((\operatorname{ListMem}\left(e, E\right)) \implies (\operatorname{NativeHolds}\left(v, e\right)))) \iff (\exists B: \operatorname{List}\left(\operatorname{BranchEquation}\left(X\right)\right), ((\operatorname{ListMem}\left(B, \operatorname{branches}\left(E\right)\right)) \land ((\forall x: X, (\operatorname{Normal}\left(\operatorname{encode}\left(\operatorname{v}\left(x\right)\right)\right))) \land ((\forall b: \operatorname{BranchEquation}\left(X\right), ((\operatorname{ListMem}\left(b, +# All named outputs and their comparison graph
+
+## Abstract
+
+Residual occurrences in a total most-general free-term substitution
+
+A presentation enumerates the entire finite family X of declared names, including unused names. C is any finite list of equations of free ordered binary terms with two distinct primitive labels. S is the actual successful result of the existing unifier from the empty substitution. Its total action assigns a term to every declared name. An unbound name is retained as its own variable. Interpreted native powers do not occur in this free-term problem. ListMem in the display denotes ordinary list membership, and sort is the third coordinate of an occurrence.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Residual positions retain their owners).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositiveImageCover.Occurrence`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositiveImageCover.Occurrence` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+An occurrence is a triple (x,p,y): the declared output name x, an ordered Boolean address p, and the residual sort y. IsOccurrence means that the subtree of the total output at x and p is exactly the variable y. The finite list occurrenceVertices enumerates every such position in every declared output; it does not restrict to names visible in the input equations.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (Edges come from every positive comparison).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositiveImageCover.occurrenceEdges`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositiveImageCover.occurrenceEdges` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+decorate gives each residual position its own occurrence label, consistently whenever a declared name is reused. comparisonTerm substitutes these decorated total outputs into each side of a supplied equation. comparisonEdges descends through corresponding constructors and records corresponding residual leaves. occurrenceEdges concatenates these finite lists over all equations, retaining their order and repetitions. Connected is the equivalence closure of this edge relation, so edges may be traversed in either direction.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (Exact finite vertices, valid edges and residual-sort components).**
+
+$$\forall X: Type, (\forall p: \operatorname{Presentation}\left(X\right), (\forall C: \operatorname{Equations}\left(X\right), (\forall S: SubstInfo, ((\operatorname{unify}\left(\operatorname{encodeEquations}\left(p, C\right), empty\right) = \operatorname{ok}\left(S\right)) \implies ((\forall o: \operatorname{Occurrence}\left(X\right), ((\operatorname{ListMem}\left(o, \operatorname{occurrenceVertices}\left(p, \operatorname{action}\left(p, S\right)\right)\right)) \iff (\operatorname{IsOccurrence}\left(\operatorname{action}\left(p, S\right), o\right)))) \land ((\forall a: \operatorname{Occurrence}\left(X\right), (\forall b: \operatorname{Occurrence}\left(X\right), ((\operatorname{ListMem}\left(\operatorname{pair}\left(a, b\right), \operatorname{occurrenceEdges}\left(C, \operatorname{action}\left(p, S\right)\right)\right)) \implies ((\operatorname{ListMem}\left(a, \operatorname{occurrenceVertices}\left(p, \operatorname{action}\left(p, S\right)\right)\right)) \land ((\operatorname{ListMem}\left(b, \operatorname{occurrenceVertices}\left(p, \operatorname{action}\left(p, S\right)\right)\right)) \land (\operatorname{sort}\left(a\right) = \operatorname{sort}\left(b\right))))))) \land (\forall a: \operatorname{Occurrence}\left(X\right), (\forall b: \operatorname{Occurrence}\left(X\right), ((\operatorname{ListMem}\left(a, \operatorname{occurrenceVertices}\left(p, \operatorname{action}\left(p, S\right)\right)\right)) \implies ((\operatorname{ListMem}\left(b, \operatorname{occurrenceVertices}\left(p, \operatorname{action}\left(p, S\right)\right)\right)) \implies ((\operatorname{Connected}\left(C, \operatorname{action}\left(p, S\right), a, b\right)) \iff (\operatorname{sort}\left(a\right) = \operatorname{sort}\left(b\right)))))))))))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositiveImageCover.mgu_occurrence_graph_exact` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every presentation, every finite equation list and every actual successful unifier result, the computed vertex list contains exactly the residual occurrences of the total action. Every computed edge joins two valid vertices of the same residual sort. Among valid vertices, connectivity is equivalent to equality of their residual sorts. Thus each occurring residual sort has exactly one connected component. There is no connectedness assertion for an empty residual sort. An unused original name contributes its own isolated residual occurrence.
+
+To prove the nontrivial direction, color the component of one occurrence by one primitive ground leaf and all other components by the other primitive ground leaf. Evaluate each decorated output with these colors. Corresponding residual positions on every positive comparison are joined by an edge, so this modified total assignment still solves all equations. The existing most-generality restriction identity forces that assignment to factor through the actual total action. At each occurrence, its color must therefore be the value of its residual sort. Two occurrences of the same sort have equal colors and hence belong to the same component. Structural traversal supplies the exact vertex and edge correspondence.
+
+This theorem concerns the free-shape stage of native positive equation elimination. It supplies no interpreted constructor/collapse reduction, rank offsets, minimum bases, executable positive image charts or full-tuple native reconstruction. Those require additional arguments; free unification is not applied directly to interpreted native equations.

+# Informationally complete pairs and forests
+
+## Abstract
+
+Two finite real random variables determine every probability weight exactly when their joint value map is injective and their bipartite fiber graph is a forest.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (The distribution on an arbitrary set).**
+
+$$\forall (\alpha: \operatorname{Type}*), ([\operatorname{Fintype}\left(\alpha\right)] [\operatorname{DecidableEq}\left(\alpha\right)], (\forall (f: \alpha \to \mathbb{R}), (\forall (\mu: \alpha \to \mathbb{R}), (\forall (\delta: \operatorname{Set}\left(\mathbb{R}\right)), ((\operatorname{D5.S3.Observer.Tomography.InformationallyCompletePairForest.distribution}\left(f, \mu, \delta\right): \mathbb{R}) = \operatorname{Finset.sum}\left(\operatorname{Finset.filter}\left(\lambda (x: \alpha) \mapsto (f\left(x\right) \in \delta), (\operatorname{Finset.univ}: \operatorname{Finset}\left(\alpha\right))\right), \lambda (x: \alpha) \mapsto (\mu\left(x\right))\right))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Observer/Tomography/InformationallyCompletePairForest.distribution` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Stan Gudder (2019). *Finite-Dimensional Convex Effect Algebras*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.1912.05110](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1912.05110). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.05110v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For a real random variable f on a finite type α and a real weight μ, the value of the distribution on δ is the sum of μ over the points whose f-values lie in δ. This is the distribution in Section 5, lines 435–439 of the TeX source, extended to arbitrary real weights and arbitrary finite types. No measurability restriction is needed on δ because the sum is finite.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (Informational completeness of a pair).**
+
+$$\forall (\alpha: \operatorname{Type}*), ([\operatorname{Fintype}\left(\alpha\right)] [\operatorname{DecidableEq}\left(\alpha\right)], (\forall (f: \alpha \to \mathbb{R}), (\forall (g: \alpha \to \mathbb{R}), ((\operatorname{D5.S3.Observer.Tomography.InformationallyCompletePairForest.IsICPair}\left(f, g\right)) \Leftrightarrow (\forall (\mu: \alpha \to \mathbb{R}), (\forall (\nu: \alpha \to \mathbb{R}), ((\operatorname{D5.S3.TotalVariation.CycleSingleCutMinimax.Probability}\left(\mu\right)) \to ((\operatorname{D5.S3.TotalVariation.CycleSingleCutMinimax.Probability}\left(\nu\right)) \to ((\operatorname{D5.S3.Observer.Tomography.InformationallyCompletePairForest.distribution}\left(f, \mu\right) = \operatorname{D5.S3.Observer.Tomography.InformationallyCompletePairForest.distribution}\left(f, \nu\right)) \to ((\operatorname{D5.S3.Observer.Tomography.InformationallyCompletePairForest.distribution}\left(g, \mu\right) = \operatorname{D5.S3.Observer.Tomography.InformationallyCompletePairForest.distribution}\left(g, \nu\right)) \to (\mu = \nu)))))))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Observer/Tomography/InformationallyCompletePairForest.IsICPair` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Stan Gudder (2019). *Finite-Dimensional Convex Effect Algebras*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.1912.05110](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1912.05110). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.05110v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The pair f, g is informationally complete if equality of both distributions forces equality of the probability weights μ and ν. Probability means that every weight is nonnegative and the sum of the weights is one. Equality of distributions is equality as functions on all subsets of the real line. This is the definition at line 474 of Section 5 of the TeX source; the finite type α may also be empty or have a single element.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (The bipartite fiber graph).**
+
+$$\forall (\alpha: \operatorname{Type}*), ([\operatorname{Fintype}\left(\alpha\right)] [\operatorname{DecidableEq}\left(\alpha\right)], (\forall (f: \alpha \to \mathbb{R}), (\forall (g: \alpha \to \mathbb{R}), ((\operatorname{D5.S3.Observer.Tomography.InformationallyCompletePairForest.fiberGraph}\left(f, g\right): \operatorname{SimpleGraph}\left(\operatorname{Sum}\left(\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{R}\right)\right)) = \operatorname{SimpleGraph.fromRel}\left(\lambda (v: \operatorname{Sum}\left(\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{R}\right)) \mapsto (\lambda (w: \operatorname{Sum}\left(\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{R}\right)) \mapsto (\operatorname{Sum.elim}\left(\lambda (a: \mathbb{R}) \mapsto (\operatorname{Sum.elim}\left(\operatorname{Function.const}\left(\mathbb{R}, \operatorname{False}\right), \lambda (b: \mathbb{R}) \mapsto (\exists (x: \alpha), ((f\left(x\right) = a) \land (g\left(x\right) = b))), w\right)), \operatorname{Function.const}\left(\mathbb{R}, \operatorname{False}\right), v\right)))\right)))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Observer/Tomography/InformationallyCompletePairForest.fiberGraph` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Stan Gudder (2019). *Finite-Dimensional Convex Effect Algebras*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.1912.05110](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1912.05110). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.05110v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The vertices are two tagged copies of the real line. A left vertex a and a right vertex b are adjacent exactly when some x has f(x) = a and g(x) = b. SimpleGraph.fromRel makes this relation symmetric and excludes loops. There are no edges within either tagged copy, and values outside the ranges of f and g are isolated vertices. Several points with the same joint value give the same simple edge; injectivity of the joint value map records the absence of that multiplicity.
+
+**Theorem 1.4 (The forest characterization).**
+
+$$\forall (\alpha: \operatorname{Type}*), ([\operatorname{Fintype}\left(\alpha\right)] [\operatorname{DecidableEq}\left(\alpha\right)], (\forall (f: \alpha \to \mathbb{R}), (\forall (g: \alpha \to \mathbb{R}), ((\operatorname{D5.S3.Observer.Tomography.InformationallyCompletePairForest.IsICPair}\left(f, g\right)) \Leftrightarrow ((\operatorname{Function.Injective}\left(\lambda (x: \alpha) \mapsto ((f\left(x\right), g\left(x\right)))\right)) \land (\operatorname{SimpleGraph.IsAcyclic}\left(\operatorname{D5.S3.Observer.Tomography.InformationallyCompletePairForest.fiberGraph}\left(f, g\right)\right)))))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Observer/Tomography/InformationallyCompletePairForest.result` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Resolves.* `Problems/gudder-2019-informationally-complete-pairs` (proved) by `D5/S3/Observer/Tomography/InformationallyCompletePairForest.result`.
+
+<!-- scribe-open-problem-resolution-v1 {"problem_slug":"gudder-2019-informationally-complete-pairs","declaration_gid":"D5/S3/Observer/Tomography/InformationallyCompletePairForest.result","resolution_kind":"proved"} -->
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Stan Gudder (2019). *Finite-Dimensional Convex Effect Algebras*. DOI: [10.48550/arXiv.1912.05110](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1912.05110). URL: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.05110v1>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The joint value map is injective exactly when every nonempty intersection of an f-level set and a g-level set is a singleton. This is complementarity in Section 5, lines 507–508 of the TeX source. The equivalence characterizes the IC pairs asked for at line 588: complementarity must be accompanied by acyclicity of the fiber graph. It holds for every finite α, including the empty and singleton cases.
+
+First, two distributions for f are equal if and only if the weights have equal sums on every f-level set. Evaluating the distributions on singletons proves necessity. For sufficiency, group the finite sum over the inverse image of any δ by the finitely many f-values occurring there, and apply equality on each level set.
+
+If the joint value map is not injective, take distinct points x and y with both f(x) = f(y) and g(x) = g(y). The point masses at x and y are distinct probabilities, but each random variable has the same distribution under the two point masses. Thus an IC pair has an injective joint value map.
+
+Assume the joint value map is injective. A trail p from u to v in the fiber graph determines a signed weight w on α. Its f-level sum at a is the indicator of u = Sum.inl(a) minus the indicator of v = Sum.inl(a); its g-level sum at b is the indicator of v = Sum.inr(b) minus the indicator of u = Sum.inr(b). Moreover, w is nonzero exactly at the points whose edges occur in p, and every absolute weight is at most one. To construct w, start with the zero weight on the empty trail. Prepending an edge from left to right adds the point mass with coefficient one at its unique point; prepending an edge from right to left adds the point mass with coefficient minus one. The trail condition keeps that edge out of the tail, so its previous weight is zero. Injectivity identifies its point uniquely, preserving the support description and the absolute bound. The marginal sums telescope to the stated endpoint indicators.
+
+Any nonzero w with absolute weights at most one and zero sums on all f-level sets and g-level sets gives distinct probabilities with equal distributions. Indeed, a nonzero coordinate makes α nonempty. Let n be its cardinality cast from a natural number to a real number, so n is positive. Summing the f-level sums gives total weight zero. Put μ(x) = (1 + w(x))/n and ν(x) = 1/n. The absolute bound makes μ nonnegative, and both total weights are one. The zero level sums make the two distributions agree for f and for g, while a nonzero coordinate of w makes μ and ν distinct.
+
+A cycle is a nonempty closed trail. Its endpoint indicators cancel, so the signed trail weight has zero sums on every level set. Some edge occurs in the cycle, and the exact support description makes this weight nonzero. The preceding perturbation then contradicts informational completeness. Combining this with injectivity proves that every IC pair has an acyclic fiber graph.
+
+Conversely, suppose the joint value map is injective and the fiber graph is acyclic. Let probabilities μ and ν have equal distributions for f and for g. For w = μ − ν, every f-level sum and every g-level sum is zero. Suppose w is nonzero, and retain only the edges arising from points where w is nonzero; call this graph H. It is a subgraph of the fiber graph and hence acyclic. Its edge set is contained in the image of finite α, so H has finitely many edges and is locally finite. A nonzero coordinate supplies an edge of H. Its connected component C contains both tagged endpoints, and is therefore a nontrivial tree with finitely many edges. Such a tree has vertices of degree one; choose one of them, u, with its unique neighbor q.
+
+The edge from u to q comes from a point y with w(y) nonzero. If u is a left vertex a, every other point z in the f-level set at a has weight zero: a nonzero weight would give another neighbor of u in C, so uniqueness of q forces g(z) = g(y), and injectivity then forces z = y. Thus the f-level sum is w(y), contradicting its vanishing. If u is a right vertex, the identical argument uses its g-level set and forces equality of the f-values. Both possibilities contradict w(y) being nonzero. Consequently w = 0, so μ = ν and the pair is IC.
+

+/- GID: D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Observer/Constructor/NativePositiveBranchReduction
+   generality: G
+   mirror-B: none(waiver:unbounded-symbolic-proof)
+   mirror-E: none(waiver:unbounded-symbolic-proof)
+   anchors: []
+   utility: none
+   digest: Finite native constructor-collapse branching and total free-shape reduction. -/
+
+import D5.S3.Arith.FibonacciAtomic.Observer.Constructor.NativePositiveImageCover
+import D5.S3.Arith.FibonacciAtomic.Observer.Constructor.NativeFiniteNormalInversion
+
+/-! Canonical native constructor cases precede free-shape unification. -/
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
+
+namespace D5.S3.Arith.FibonacciAtomic.Observer.NativePositiveBranchReduction
+
+open NativeFiniteNormalInversion (Code Normal expand encode smart shiftCode)
+open NativeTermUnification (Term Presentation evaluate)
+open NativeGroundSolutionSpace (Sol action encodeEquations)
+open NativePositiveImageCover (Occurrence occurrenceVertices Connected occurrenceEdges comparisonEdges
+  comparisonTerm mgu_occurrence_graph_exact)
+open GenealogicalFiberTransport (substitution)
+open Lambda Strata.Util
+
+abbrev Source := GenealogicalFiberTransport.Source
+
+variable {X : Type}
+
+/-- Finite named native equations. Every declared name remains in X. -/
+inductive Equation (X : Type) where
+  | primitive : X → Nat → Equation X
+  | shift : X → Nat → X → Equation X
+  | pair : X → X → X → Equation X
+  | same : X → X → Equation X
+
+def Equation.Holds (v : X → Source) : Equation X → Prop
+  | .primitive z n => v z = expand (.of n)
+  | .shift z a x => v z = substitution^[a] (v x)
+  | .pair z x y => v z = .mul (v x) (v y)
+  | .same x y => v x = v y
+
+/-- A collapse introduces an unrestricted natural rank, rather than
+enumerating ranks or bounding the underlying source trees. -/
+inductive BranchEquation (X : Type) where
+  | primitive : X → Nat → BranchEquation X
+  | shift : X → Nat → X → BranchEquation X
+  | ordinary : X → X → X → BranchEquation X
+  | collapse : X → X → X → BranchEquation X
+  | same : X → X → BranchEquation X
+
+def BranchEquation.origin : BranchEquation X → Equation X
+  | .primitive z n => .primitive z n
+  | .shift z a x => .shift z a x
+  | .ordinary z x y | .collapse z x y => .pair z x y
+  | .same x y => .same x y
+
+def BranchEquation.Holds (u : X → Code) : BranchEquation X → Prop
+  | .primitive z n => u z = .of n
+  | .shift z a x => u z = shiftCode a (u x)
+  | .ordinary z x y => u z = .mul (u x) (u y)
+  | .collapse z x y => ∃ r : Nat,
+      u x = .of (r + 1) ∧ u y = .of r ∧ u z = .of (r + 2)
+  | .same x y => u x = u y
+
+def choices : Equation X → List (BranchEquation X)
+  | .primitive z n => [.primitive z n]
+  | .shift z a x => [.shift z a x]
+  | .pair z x y => [.ordinary z x y, .collapse z x y]
+  | .same x y => [.same x y]
+
+/-- Executable finite branching depends only on the input equations. -/
+def branches : List (Equation X) → List (List (BranchEquation X))
+  | [] => [[]]
+  | e :: E => (choices e).flatMap fun b => (branches E).map (b :: ·)
+
+/-- Erase only ranks, after choosing the native constructor cases. -/
+def shape : Code → Source
+  | .of _ => .of true
+  | .mul l r => .mul (shape l) (shape r)
+
+private def name (x : X) : Term X := .of (.inr x)
+private def shapeLeaf : Term X := .of (.inl true)
+
+def BranchEquation.shapeEquations : BranchEquation X → NativeGroundSolutionSpace.Equations X
+  | .primitive z _ => [(name z, shapeLeaf)]
+  | .shift z _ x => [(name z, name x)]
+  | .ordinary z x y => [(name z, .mul (name x) (name y))]
+  | .collapse z x y => [(name x, shapeLeaf), (name y, shapeLeaf), (name z, shapeLeaf)]
+  | .same x y => [(name x, name y)]
+
+def shapeEquations (B : List (BranchEquation X)) : NativeGroundSolutionSpace.Equations X :=
+  B.flatMap BranchEquation.shapeEquations
+
+/-! The source-side comparison carrier keeps the rank information that is
+discarded by `shape`.  A shift contributes its actual natural offset, while
+ordinary and equality comparisons contribute zero offset.  Primitive and
+collapse cases retain their scalar constraints in `B` but contribute no
+residual block edge. -/
+
+private def offsetComparisonEdges (d : Int) : Term (Occurrence X) → Term (Occurrence X) →
+    List ((Occurrence X × Occurrence X) × Int)
+  | .of (.inr a), .of (.inr b) => [((a, b), d)]
+  | .mul l r, .mul u v => offsetComparisonEdges d l u ++ offsetComparisonEdges d r v
+  | _, _ => []
+
+private theorem offsetComparisonEdges_projection (d : Int)
+    (A B : Term (Occurrence X)) :
+    (offsetComparisonEdges d A B).map (fun e => e.1) = comparisonEdges A B := by
+  induction A generalizing B with
+  | of a =>
+      cases B with
+      | of b => cases a <;> cases b <;> rfl
+      | mul l r => simp [offsetComparisonEdges, comparisonEdges]
+  | mul l r hl hr =>
+      cases B with
+      | of a => rfl
+      | mul u v =>
+          simp only [offsetComparisonEdges, comparisonEdges, List.map_append, hl, hr]
+
+def sourceOffsetEdges (B : List (BranchEquation X)) (s : X → Term X) :
+    List ((Occurrence X × Occurrence X) × Int) :=
+  B.flatMap fun b => match b with
+  | .primitive _ _ => []
+  | .shift z a x =>
+      offsetComparisonEdges (Int.ofNat a)
+        (comparisonTerm s (name z)) (comparisonTerm s (name x))
+  | .ordinary z x y =>
+      offsetComparisonEdges 0
+        (comparisonTerm s (name z))
+        (comparisonTerm s (.mul (name x) (name y)))
+  | .collapse _ _ _ => []
+  | .same x y =>
+      offsetComparisonEdges 0
+        (comparisonTerm s (name x)) (comparisonTerm s (name y))
+
+def sourceOccurrenceEdges (B : List (BranchEquation X)) (s : X → Term X) :
+    List (Occurrence X × Occurrence X) :=
+  (sourceOffsetEdges B s).map (fun e => e.1)
+
+def sourceConnected (B : List (BranchEquation X)) (s : X → Term X) :
+    Occurrence X → Occurrence X → Prop :=
+  Relation.EqvGen (fun a b => (a, b) ∈ sourceOccurrenceEdges B s)
+
+private theorem comparisonTerm_primitive_leaf (s : X → Term X) :
+    comparisonTerm s (.of (.inl true) : Term X) =
+      (.of (.inl true) : Term (Occurrence X)) := by
+  rfl
+
+private theorem comparisonEdges_primitive_right (A : Term (Occurrence X)) (b : Bool) :
+    comparisonEdges A (.of (.inl b)) = [] := by
+  cases A with
+  | of a => cases a <;> rfl
+  | mul l r => rfl
+
+theorem source_comparison_graph_identification (B : List (BranchEquation X))
+    (s : X → Term X) :
+    sourceOccurrenceEdges B s = occurrenceEdges (shapeEquations B) s := by
+  induction B with
+  | nil => rfl
+  | cons b B ih =>
+      have head :
+          (sourceOffsetEdges [b] s).map (fun e => e.1) =
+            occurrenceEdges (BranchEquation.shapeEquations b) s := by
+        cases b <;>
+          simp [sourceOffsetEdges, occurrenceEdges, BranchEquation.shapeEquations,
+            offsetComparisonEdges_projection, comparisonEdges,
+            name, shapeLeaf]
+        all_goals
+          simp [comparisonTerm_primitive_leaf, comparisonEdges_primitive_right]
+      calc
+        sourceOccurrenceEdges (b :: B) s =
+            (sourceOffsetEdges [b] s).map (fun e => e.1) ++
+              sourceOccurrenceEdges B s := by
+                change (sourceOffsetEdges (b :: B) s).map (fun e => e.1) =
+                  (sourceOffsetEdges [b] s).map (fun e => e.1) ++
+                    (sourceOffsetEdges B s).map (fun e => e.1)
+                simp [sourceOffsetEdges, List.flatMap_cons, List.map_append,
+                  List.flatMap_singleton]
+        _ = occurrenceEdges (BranchEquation.shapeEquations b) s ++
+              occurrenceEdges (shapeEquations B) s := by rw [head, ih]
+        _ = occurrenceEdges (shapeEquations (b :: B)) s := by
+              simp only [shapeEquations, List.flatMap_cons, occurrenceEdges,
+                List.flatMap_append]
+
+theorem source_connected_iff_sort (p : Presentation X)
+    (B : List (BranchEquation X)) (S : SubstInfo)
+    (hok : (encodeEquations p (shapeEquations B)).unify SubstInfo.empty = .ok S)
+    (a b : Occurrence X)
+    (ha : a ∈ occurrenceVertices p (action p S))
+    (hb : b ∈ occurrenceVertices p (action p S)) :
+    (sourceConnected B (action p S) a b ↔ a.2.2 = b.2.2) := by
+  unfold sourceConnected
+  rw [source_comparison_graph_identification]
+  exact (mgu_occurrence_graph_exact p (shapeEquations B) S hok).2.2 a b ha hb
+
+private theorem shift_smart (a : Nat) (A B : Code) :
+    smart (shiftCode a A) (shiftCode a B) = shiftCode a (smart A B) := by
+  cases A with
+  | of n =>
+      cases B with
+      | of m =>
+          have eq : n + a = m + a + 1 ↔ n = m + 1 := by omega
+          simp only [shiftCode, smart, eq]
+          split_ifs <;> congr 1 <;> omega
+      | mul l r => rfl
+  | mul l r => cases B <;> rfl
+
+private theorem encode_substitution (g : Source) :
+    encode (substitution g) = shiftCode 1 (encode g) := by
+  induction g with
+  | of b => cases b <;> rfl
+  | mul l r hl hr =>
+      change smart (encode (substitution l)) (encode (substitution r)) = _
+      rw [hl, hr]
+      exact shift_smart 1 (encode l) (encode r)
+
+private theorem shift_zero (C : Code) : shiftCode 0 C = C := by
+  induction C with
+  | of n => rfl
+  | mul l r hl hr => exact congrArg₂ FreeMagma.mul hl hr
+
+private theorem shift_add (a b : Nat) (C : Code) :
+    shiftCode a (shiftCode b C) = shiftCode (a + b) C := by
+  induction C with
+  | of n => simp only [shiftCode, Nat.add_assoc, Nat.add_comm b a]
+  | mul l r hl hr => exact congrArg₂ FreeMagma.mul hl hr
+
+private theorem encode_shift (a : Nat) (g : Source) :
+    encode (substitution^[a] g) = shiftCode a (encode g) := by
+  induction a with
+  | zero => exact (shift_zero _).symm
+  | succ a ih =>
+      rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', encode_substitution, ih, shift_add]
+      congr 1
+      omega
+
+private theorem encode_primitive (n : Nat) : encode (expand (.of n)) = .of n := by
+  change encode (substitution^[n] (.of true)) = .of n
+  rw [encode_shift]
+  simp only [encode, shiftCode, Nat.zero_add]
+
+private theorem choice_complete (e : Equation X) (v : X → Source) (h : e.Holds v) :
+    ∃ b ∈ choices e, b.Holds (fun x => encode (v x)) := by
+  cases e with
+  | primitive z n =>
+      refine ⟨.primitive z n, List.mem_singleton_self _, ?_⟩
+      change encode (v z) = .of n
+      rw [h, encode_primitive]
+  | shift z a x =>
+      refine ⟨.shift z a x, List.mem_singleton_self _, ?_⟩
+      change encode (v z) = shiftCode a (encode (v x))
+      rw [h, encode_shift]
+  | same x y =>
+      exact ⟨.same x y, List.mem_singleton_self _, congrArg encode h⟩
+  | pair z x y =>
+      have hz : encode (v z) = smart (encode (v x)) (encode (v y)) := by
+        rw [h]
+        rfl
+      cases hx : encode (v x) with
+      | of n =>
+          cases hy : encode (v y) with
+          | of m =>
+              by_cases eq : n = m + 1
+              · refine ⟨.collapse z x y, by simp [choices], m, ?_, hy, ?_⟩
+                · simpa only [eq] using hx
+                · simpa only [hx, hy, smart, eq, ite_true] using hz
+              · refine ⟨.ordinary z x y, by simp [choices], ?_⟩
+                simpa only [BranchEquation.Holds, hx, hy, smart, eq, ite_false] using hz
+          | mul l r =>
+              refine ⟨.ordinary z x y, by simp [choices], ?_⟩
+              simpa only [BranchEquation.Holds, hx, hy, smart] using hz
+      | mul l r =>
+          refine ⟨.ordinary z x y, by simp [choices], ?_⟩
+          cases hy : encode (v y) <;> simpa only [BranchEquation.Holds, hx, hy, smart] using hz
+
+private theorem branch_sound (u : X → Code) (b : BranchEquation X) (h : b.Holds u) :
+    b.origin.Holds (fun x => expand (u x)) := by
+  cases b with
+  | primitive z n => exact congrArg expand h
+  | shift z a x =>
+      change expand (u z) = substitution^[a] (expand (u x))
+      rw [h, NativeFiniteNormalInversion.shift_expand]
+  | ordinary z x y => exact congrArg expand h
+  | same x y => exact congrArg expand h
+  | collapse z x y =>
+      obtain ⟨r,hx,hy,hz⟩ := h
+      change expand (u z) = .mul (expand (u x)) (expand (u y))
+      rw [hx, hy, hz]
+      exact NativeRankedEqualityCompiler.atomic_pair r
+
+private theorem choices_origin (e : Equation X) (b : BranchEquation X) (h : b ∈ choices e) :
+    b.origin = e := by
+  cases e <;> simp only [choices, List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at h
+  all_goals first
+    | subst b; rfl
+    | rcases h with rfl | rfl <;> rfl
+
+private theorem branches_exact (E : List (Equation X)) (v : X → Source) :
+    (∀ e ∈ E, e.Holds v) ↔

+  induction E with
+  | nil => simp [branches]
+  | cons e E ih =>
+      constructor

+        · exact tail c hc

+private theorem shape_shift (a : Nat) (C : Code) : shape (shiftCode a C) = shape C := by
+  induction C with
+  | of n => rfl
+  | mul l r hl hr => exact congrArg₂ FreeMagma.mul hl hr

+private theorem branch_shape (u : X → Code) (b : BranchEquation X) (h : b.Holds u) :
+    Sol b.shapeEquations (fun x => shape (u x)) := by
+  cases b with
+  | primitive z n =>
+      intro c hc
+      simp only [BranchEquation.shapeEquations, List.mem_singleton] at hc
+      subst c
+      change shape (u z) = .of true
+      rw [h]
+      rfl
+  | shift z a x =>
+      intro c hc
+      simp only [BranchEquation.shapeEquations, List.mem_singleton] at hc
+      subst c
+      change shape (u z) = shape (u x)
+      rw [h, shape_shift]
+  | ordinary z x y =>
+      intro c hc
+      simp only [BranchEquation.shapeEquations, List.mem_singleton] at hc
+      subst c
+      change shape (u z) = .mul (shape (u x)) (shape (u y))
+      rw [h]
+      rfl
+  | same x y =>
+      intro c hc
+      simp only [BranchEquation.shapeEquations, List.mem_singleton] at hc
+      subst c

+  | collapse z x y =>
+      obtain ⟨r,hx,hy,hz⟩ := h
+      intro c hc

+        rw [hx]; rfl
+      · change shape (u y) = .of true
+        rw [hy]; rfl
+      · change shape (u z) = .of true
+        rw [hz]; rfl

+/-- Every actual solution selects a member of the executable finite branch

+theorem native_branch_reduction (p : Presentation X) (E : List (Equation X)) (v : X → Source) :

+        NativeGroundSolutionSpace.evaluate_restrictTerm] using eq

+    · exact source_connected_iff_sort p B S hok
+  · rintro ⟨B,hB,_,sat,S,hok,_,_,_⟩
+    exact (branches_exact E v).mpr ⟨B,hB,sat⟩
+
+end D5.S3.Arith.FibonacciAtomic.Observer.NativePositiveBranchReduction

+import D5.S3.Arith.FibonacciAtomic.Observer.NativeGroundSolutionSpace
+import Mathlib.Logic.Relation

+/-! The free-shape prerequisite for positive native image covers. The unifier
+is applied only to free Boolean constructor terms. Interpreted native powers,
+rank offsets and the entire image-cover construction are separate obligations. -/
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
+
+namespace D5.S3.Arith.FibonacciAtomic.Observer.NativePositiveImageCover
+
+open Lambda Strata.Util NativeTermUnification
+open NativeGroundSolutionSpace
+
+abbrev Source := NativeGroundSolutionSpace.Source
+
+variable {X : Type}
+
+/-- A residual occurrence retains its declared output name, ordered address
+and residual sort. Validity is checked against that total output. -/
+abbrev Occurrence (X : Type) := X × List Bool × X
+
+def subtree {A : Type} : FreeMagma A → List Bool → Option (FreeMagma A)
+  | t, [] => some t
+  | .of _, _ :: _ => none
+  | .mul l _, false :: q => subtree l q
+  | .mul _ r, true :: q => subtree r q
+
+def IsOccurrence (s : X → Term X) (o : Occurrence X) : Prop :=
+  subtree (s o.1) o.2.1 = some (.of (.inr o.2.2))
+
+/-- Each use of a declared name receives the same occurrence labels. -/
+def decorateFrom (x : X) (p : List Bool) : Term X → Term (Occurrence X)
+  | .of (.inl b) => .of (.inl b)
+  | .of (.inr y) => .of (.inr (x, p, y))
+  | .mul l r => .mul (decorateFrom x (p ++ [false]) l)
+      (decorateFrom x (p ++ [true]) r)
+
+def decorate (s : X → Term X) (x : X) : Term (Occurrence X) :=
+  decorateFrom x [] (s x)
+
+private def erase : Term (Occurrence X) → Term X
+  | .of (.inl b) => .of (.inl b)
+  | .of (.inr o) => .of (.inr o.2.2)
+  | .mul l r => .mul (erase l) (erase r)
+
+private def instantiate {A B : Type} (s : A → Term B) : Term A → Term B :=
+  FreeMagma.lift (Sum.elim (fun b => .of (.inl b)) s)
+
+/-- Expand all names before matching positive comparisons. -/
+def comparisonTerm (s : X → Term X) (t : Term X) : Term (Occurrence X) :=
+  instantiate (decorate s) t
+
+/-- Match only corresponding residual leaves. Ordinary constructors and
+explicit primitive leaves contribute no block edge. -/
+def comparisonEdges : Term (Occurrence X) → Term (Occurrence X) →
+    List (Occurrence X × Occurrence X)
+  | .of (.inr a), .of (.inr b) => [(a,b)]
+  | .mul l r, .mul u v => comparisonEdges l u ++ comparisonEdges r v
+  | _, _ => []
+
+def occurrenceEdges (C : Equations X) (s : X → Term X) :
+    List (Occurrence X × Occurrence X) :=
+  C.flatMap fun c => comparisonEdges (comparisonTerm s c.1) (comparisonTerm s c.2)
+
+/-- Every declared output is included, even when its name is absent from C.
+Repeated occurrences remain distinct vertices. -/
+def occurrenceVertices (p : Presentation X) (s : X → Term X) : List (Occurrence X) :=
+  p.enumeration.flatMap fun x => termVars (decorate s x)
+
+def Connected (C : Equations X) (s : X → Term X) :
+    Occurrence X → Occurrence X → Prop :=
+  Relation.EqvGen (fun a b => (a,b) ∈ occurrenceEdges C s)
+
+private theorem erase_decorateFrom (x : X) (p : List Bool) (t : Term X) :
+    erase (decorateFrom x p t) = t := by
+  induction t generalizing p with
+  | of a => cases a <;> rfl
+  | mul l r hl hr => exact congrArg₂ FreeMagma.mul (hl _) (hr _)
+
+private theorem erase_comparison (s : X → Term X) (t : Term X) :
+    erase (comparisonTerm s t) = substitute s t := by
+  induction t with
+  | of a => cases a with
+    | inl b => rfl
+    | inr x => exact erase_decorateFrom x [] (s x)
+  | mul l r hl hr => exact congrArg₂ FreeMagma.mul hl hr
+
+private theorem instantiate_evaluate {A B : Type} (s : A → Term B)
+    (v : B → Source) (t : Term A) :
+    evaluate v (instantiate s t) = evaluate (fun x => evaluate v (s x)) t := by
+  induction t with
+  | of a => cases a <;> rfl
+  | mul l r hl hr => exact congrArg₂ FreeMagma.mul hl hr
+
+private theorem decorate_subtree (x : X) (p q : List Bool) (t : Term X) (y : X)
+    (h : subtree t q = some (.of (.inr y))) :
+    subtree (decorateFrom x p t) q = some (.of (.inr (x,p ++ q,y))) := by
+  induction q generalizing p t with
+  | nil =>
+      simp only [subtree, Option.some.injEq] at h
+      subst t
+      simp only [decorateFrom, subtree, List.append_nil]
+  | cons b q ih =>
+      cases t with
+      | of a => cases h
+      | mul l r =>
+          cases b
+          · simpa only [decorateFrom, subtree, List.append_assoc, List.cons_append,
+              List.nil_append] using ih (p ++ [false]) l h
+          · simpa only [decorateFrom, subtree, List.append_assoc, List.cons_append,
+              List.nil_append] using ih (p ++ [true]) r h
+
+private theorem evaluate_subtree {A : Type} (v : A → Source)
+    (t : Term A) (q : List Bool) (y : A)
+    (h : subtree t q = some (.of (.inr y))) :
+    subtree (evaluate v t) q = some (v y) := by
+  induction q generalizing t with
+  | nil =>
+      simp only [subtree, Option.some.injEq] at h
+      subst t
+      simp only [subtree, evaluate, FreeMagma.lift_of, Sum.elim_inr]
+  | cons b q ih =>
+      cases t with
+      | of a => cases h
+      | mul l r => cases b <;> exact ih _ h
+
+private theorem comparison_edge_at (A B : Term (Occurrence X)) (q : List Bool)
+    (a b : Occurrence X)
+    (ha : subtree A q = some (.of (.inr a)))
+    (hb : subtree B q = some (.of (.inr b))) :
+    (a,b) ∈ comparisonEdges A B := by
+  induction q generalizing A B with
+  | nil =>
+      simp only [subtree, Option.some.injEq] at ha hb
+      subst A; subst B
+      exact List.mem_singleton_self _
+  | cons d q ih =>
+      cases A with
+      | of c => cases ha
+      | mul l r =>
+          cases B with
+          | of c => cases hb
+          | mul u v =>
+              cases d
+              · exact List.mem_append_left _ (ih l u ha hb)
+              · exact List.mem_append_right _ (ih r v ha hb)
+
+private theorem comparison_evaluate (A B : Term (Occurrence X))
+    (v : Occurrence X → Source) (he : erase A = erase B)
+    (hv : ∀ q a b, subtree A q = some (.of (.inr a)) →
+      subtree B q = some (.of (.inr b)) → v a = v b) :
+    evaluate v A = evaluate v B := by
+  induction A generalizing B with
+  | of a =>
+      cases B with
+      | of b =>
+          cases a with
+          | inl c =>
+              cases b with
+              | inl d =>
+                  have cd : c = d := by injection he with h; exact Sum.inl.inj h
+                  subst d; rfl
+              | inr o => cases he
+          | inr o =>
+              cases b with
+              | inl d => cases he
+              | inr u => exact hv [] o u rfl rfl
+      | mul l r => cases a <;> cases he
+  | mul l r hl hr =>
+      cases B with
+      | of b => cases b <;> cases he
+      | mul u w =>
+          have parts : erase l = erase u ∧ erase r = erase w := by
+            injection he with h1 h2; exact ⟨h1,h2⟩
+          exact congrArg₂ FreeMagma.mul
+            (hl u parts.1 (fun q a b ha hb => hv (false :: q) a b ha hb))
+            (hr w parts.2 (fun q a b ha hb => hv (true :: q) a b ha hb))
+
+private theorem unified_comparison (p : Presentation X) (C : Equations X)
+    (S : SubstInfo) (hok : (encodeEquations p C).unify SubstInfo.empty = .ok S)
+    (c : Term X × Term X) (hc : c ∈ C) :
+    erase (comparisonTerm (action p S) c.1) =
+      erase (comparisonTerm (action p S) c.2) := by
+  have native := Constraints.unify_sound (encodeEquations p C) SubstInfo.empty S hok
+    (encode p c.1, encode p c.2) (List.mem_map.mpr ⟨c,hc,rfl⟩)
+  have eqs : substitute (action p S) c.1 = substitute (action p S) c.2 := by
+    apply encode_injective p
+    simpa only [action_substitute_encode p C S hok] using native
+  rw [erase_comparison, erase_comparison, eqs]
+
+/-- In the actual total MGU of any finite free constructor problem, any two
+occurrences of the same residual sort are connected by positive comparisons.
+There is no assertion about an empty, unused residual sort. -/
+private theorem same_sort_connected (p : Presentation X) (C : Equations X)
+    (S : SubstInfo) (hok : (encodeEquations p C).unify SubstInfo.empty = .ok S)

+private theorem subtree_var_mem {A : Type} (t : Term A) (q : List Bool) (y : A)
+    (h : subtree t q = some (.of (.inr y))) : y ∈ termVars t := by
+  induction q generalizing t with
+  | nil =>
+      simp only [subtree, Option.some.injEq] at h
+      subst t
+      exact List.mem_singleton_self _
+  | cons b q ih =>
+      cases t with
+      | of a => cases h
+      | mul l r =>
+          cases b
+          · exact List.mem_append_left _ (ih l h)
+          · exact List.mem_append_right _ (ih r h)
+
+private theorem decorated_vars (x : X) (p : List Bool) (t : Term X)
+    (o : Occurrence X) (ho : o ∈ termVars (decorateFrom x p t)) :
+    ∃ y q, o = (x,p ++ q,y) ∧ subtree t q = some (.of (.inr y)) := by
+  induction t generalizing p with
+  | of a =>
+      cases a with
+      | inl b => cases ho
+      | inr y =>
+          refine ⟨y, [], ?_, rfl⟩
+          simpa only [decorateFrom, termVars, List.mem_singleton, List.append_nil] using ho
+  | mul l r hl hr =>
+      rcases List.mem_append.mp ho with ho | ho
+      · obtain ⟨y,q,eq,hq⟩ := hl (p ++ [false]) ho
+        refine ⟨y,false :: q,?_,hq⟩
+        simpa only [List.append_assoc, List.cons_append, List.nil_append] using eq
+      · obtain ⟨y,q,eq,hq⟩ := hr (p ++ [true]) ho
+        refine ⟨y,true :: q,?_,hq⟩
+        simpa only [List.append_assoc, List.cons_append, List.nil_append] using eq
+
+private theorem vertex_spec (p : Presentation X) (s : X → Term X) (o : Occurrence X) :
+    o ∈ occurrenceVertices p s ↔ IsOccurrence s o := by
+  constructor
+  · intro h
+    obtain ⟨x,_,ho⟩ := List.mem_flatMap.mp h
+    obtain ⟨y,q,rfl,hq⟩ := decorated_vars x [] (s x) o ho
+    simpa only [IsOccurrence, List.nil_append] using hq
+  · intro h
+    refine List.mem_flatMap.mpr ⟨o.1,p.complete o.1,?_⟩
+    apply subtree_var_mem (decorate s o.1) o.2.1 o
+    simpa only [decorate, List.nil_append] using
+      decorate_subtree o.1 [] o.2.1 (s o.1) o.2.2 h
+
+private theorem comparison_vars_valid (s : X → Term X) (t : Term X)
+    (o : Occurrence X) (h : o ∈ termVars (comparisonTerm s t)) : IsOccurrence s o := by
+  induction t with
+  | of a =>
+      cases a with
+      | inl b => cases h
+      | inr x =>
+          obtain ⟨y,q,rfl,hq⟩ := decorated_vars x [] (s x) o h
+          simpa only [IsOccurrence, List.nil_append] using hq
+  | mul l r hl hr =>
+      rcases List.mem_append.mp h with h | h
+      · exact hl h
+      · exact hr h
+
+private theorem erase_subtree (t : Term (Occurrence X)) (q : List Bool) (o : Occurrence X)
+    (h : subtree t q = some (.of (.inr o))) :
+    subtree (erase t) q = some (.of (.inr o.2.2)) := by
+  induction q generalizing t with
+  | nil =>
+      simp only [subtree, Option.some.injEq] at h
+      subst t
+      rfl
+  | cons b q ih =>
+      cases t with
+      | of a => cases h
+      | mul l r => cases b <;> exact ih _ h
+
+private theorem edge_position (A B : Term (Occurrence X)) (a b : Occurrence X)
+    (h : (a,b) ∈ comparisonEdges A B) :
+    ∃ q, subtree A q = some (.of (.inr a)) ∧ subtree B q = some (.of (.inr b)) := by
+  induction A generalizing B with
+  | of c =>
+      cases c with
+      | inl c => cases B <;> simp [comparisonEdges] at h
+      | inr o =>
+          cases B with
+          | of d =>
+              cases d with
+              | inl d => cases h
+              | inr u =>
+                  simp only [comparisonEdges, List.mem_singleton, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
+                  rcases h with ⟨rfl,rfl⟩
+                  exact ⟨[],rfl,rfl⟩
+          | mul l r => cases h
+  | mul l r hl hr =>
+      cases B with
+      | of d => cases d <;> cases h
+      | mul u v =>
+          rcases List.mem_append.mp h with h | h
+          · obtain ⟨q,ha,hb⟩ := hl u h
+            exact ⟨false :: q,ha,hb⟩
+          · obtain ⟨q,ha,hb⟩ := hr v h
+            exact ⟨true :: q,ha,hb⟩
+
+private theorem edge_spec (p : Presentation X) (C : Equations X) (S : SubstInfo)
+    (hok : (encodeEquations p C).unify SubstInfo.empty = .ok S)
+    (a b : Occurrence X) (h : (a,b) ∈ occurrenceEdges C (action p S)) :
+    IsOccurrence (action p S) a ∧ IsOccurrence (action p S) b ∧ a.2.2 = b.2.2 := by
+  obtain ⟨c,hc,edge⟩ := List.mem_flatMap.mp h
+  obtain ⟨q,ha,hb⟩ := edge_position _ _ a b edge
+  refine ⟨comparison_vars_valid _ _ a (subtree_var_mem _ q a ha),
+    comparison_vars_valid _ _ b (subtree_var_mem _ q b hb), ?_⟩
+  have h1 := erase_subtree _ q a ha
+  have h2 := erase_subtree _ q b hb
+  rw [unified_comparison p C S hok c hc] at h1
+  have same := Option.some.inj (h1.symm.trans h2)
+  injection same with same
+  exact Sum.inr.inj same
+
+/-- The computed finite graph contains exactly all residual occurrences in
+the total MGU outputs. Its edges join valid occurrences of the same sort,
+and two valid vertices are connected exactly when their sorts agree. -/
+theorem mgu_occurrence_graph_exact (p : Presentation X) (C : Equations X)
+    (S : SubstInfo) (hok : (encodeEquations p C).unify SubstInfo.empty = .ok S) :
+    (∀ o, o ∈ occurrenceVertices p (action p S) ↔ IsOccurrence (action p S) o) ∧
+    (∀ a b, (a,b) ∈ occurrenceEdges C (action p S) →
+      a ∈ occurrenceVertices p (action p S) ∧ b ∈ occurrenceVertices p (action p S) ∧
+        a.2.2 = b.2.2) ∧

+/-!
+# Informationally complete pairs and forests
+
+For finite real random variables, the two pushforward distributions determine every
+probability weight precisely when the joint value map is injective and its bipartite
+fiber graph is acyclic. Complementarity means injectivity of the joint value map.
+
+A signed trail weight has marginal sums supported at its endpoints. A cycle therefore
+produces a nonzero weight with zero marginals; perturbing the uniform probability by
+this bounded weight gives two distinct probabilities with the same distributions.
+Conversely, the nonzero support of a difference with zero marginals cannot have a leaf,
+whereas every nontrivial finite tree has one.
+
+The probability and completeness notions are those of Section 5 of S. Gudder,
+*Finite-Dimensional Convex Effect Algebras* (arXiv:1912.05110v1).
+-/
+
+noncomputable section
+open scoped BigOperators
+open D5.S3.TotalVariation.CycleSingleCutMinimax (Probability)
+
+namespace D5.S3.Observer.Tomography.InformationallyCompletePairForest
+
+open Classical in
+/-- The distribution of a real random variable, evaluated on an arbitrary set. -/
+def distribution {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    (f : α → ℝ) (μ : α → ℝ) (δ : Set ℝ) : ℝ :=
+  ∑ x ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun x => f x ∈ δ), μ x
+
+/-- The two marginal distributions determine every probability weight uniquely. -/
+def IsICPair {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (f g : α → ℝ) : Prop :=
+  ∀ μ ν, Probability μ → Probability ν →
+    distribution f μ = distribution f ν → distribution g μ = distribution g ν → μ = ν
+
+/-- A point supplies an edge between its two tagged random-variable values. -/
+def fiberGraph {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] (f g : α → ℝ) : SimpleGraph (ℝ ⊕ ℝ) :=
+  SimpleGraph.fromRel (fun v w =>
+    Sum.elim (fun a => Sum.elim (fun _ => False)
+      (fun b => ∃ x, f x = a ∧ g x = b) w) (fun _ => False) v)
+
+private def supportGraph {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    (f g w : α → ℝ) : SimpleGraph (ℝ ⊕ ℝ) :=
+  SimpleGraph.fromRel (fun v z =>
+    Sum.elim (fun a => Sum.elim (fun _ => False)
+      (fun b => ∃ x, f x = a ∧ g x = b ∧ w x ≠ 0) z) (fun _ => False) v)
+
+private lemma supportGraph_edge_finite {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    (f g w : α → ℝ) : (supportGraph f g w).edgeSet.Finite := by
+  classical
+  apply (Set.finite_range (fun x : α => s(Sum.inl (f x), Sum.inr (g x)))).subset
+  intro e he
+  induction e using Sym2.inductionOn with
+  | _ v z =>
+    rw [SimpleGraph.mem_edgeSet] at he
+    have he' := (SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj _ _ _).mp he
+    rcases he'.2 with hrel | hrel
+    · rcases v with a | a
+      · rcases z with b | b
+        · dsimp only [supportGraph] at *
+          simp_all
+        · rcases hrel with ⟨x, hfx, hgx, hw⟩
+          refine ⟨x, ?_⟩
+          simp [hfx, hgx]
+      · rcases z with b | b <;> dsimp only [supportGraph] at * <;> simp_all
+    · rcases v with a | a
+      · rcases z with b | b <;> dsimp only [supportGraph] at * <;> simp_all
+      · rcases z with b | b
+        · rcases hrel with ⟨x, hfx, hgx, hw⟩
+          refine ⟨x, ?_⟩
+          simp [hfx, hgx]
+        · dsimp only [supportGraph] at *
+          simp_all
+
+@[instance_reducible]
+private noncomputable def locallyFinite_of_finite_edgeSet {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V)
+    [Finite G.edgeSet] : G.LocallyFinite := by
+  classical
+  intro v
+  letI : Fintype (G.incidenceSet v) :=
+    ((Set.toFinite G.edgeSet).subset (G.incidenceSet_subset v)).fintype
+  exact Fintype.ofEquiv (G.incidenceSet v) (G.incidenceSetEquivNeighborSet v)
+
+private lemma finite_component_edgeSet {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V)
+    [Finite G.edgeSet] (C : G.ConnectedComponent) : Finite C.toSimpleGraph.edgeSet := by
+  exact Finite.of_injective (SimpleGraph.Embedding.induce C.supp).mapEdgeSet
+    (SimpleGraph.Embedding.induce C.supp).mapEdgeSet.injective
+
+private lemma distribution_eq_iff_fiber_sums {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    (f : α → ℝ) (μ ν : α → ℝ) :
+    distribution f μ = distribution f ν ↔
+      ∀ a, (∑ x ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun x => f x = a), μ x) =
+        ∑ x ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun x => f x = a), ν x := by
+  classical
+  constructor
+  · intro h a
+    have ha := congrFun h ({a} : Set ℝ)
+    have hμ : distribution f μ ({a} : Set ℝ) =
+        ∑ x ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun x => f x = a), μ x := by
+      unfold distribution
+      simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff]
+    have hν : distribution f ν ({a} : Set ℝ) =
+        ∑ x ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun x => f x = a), ν x := by
+      unfold distribution
+      simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff]
+    rw [hμ, hν] at ha
+    exact ha
+  · intro h
+    funext δ
+    let s : Finset α := Finset.univ.filter (fun x => f x ∈ δ)
+    let t : Finset ℝ := s.image f
+    have hmap : ∀ x ∈ s, f x ∈ t := by
+      intro x hx
+      exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
+    have hμ := Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to hmap μ
+    have hν := Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to hmap ν
+    have hfiber (a : ℝ) (ha : a ∈ t) (q : α → ℝ) :
+        (∑ x ∈ s with f x = a, q x) =
+          ∑ x ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun x => f x = a), q x := by
+      obtain ⟨x, hx, hxa⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp ha
+      have hδa : f x ∈ δ := by simpa [s] using hx
+      have hδa' : a ∈ δ := by simpa [hxa] using hδa
+      apply Finset.sum_congr
+      · ext y
+        simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, s]
+        constructor
+        · rintro ⟨hfd, hfa⟩
+          exact hfa
+        · intro hfa
+          exact ⟨by simpa [hfa] using hδa', hfa⟩
+      · intro y hy
+        rfl
+    calc
+      distribution f μ δ = ∑ x ∈ s, μ x := rfl
+      _ = ∑ a ∈ t, ∑ x ∈ s with f x = a, μ x := hμ.symm
+      _ = ∑ a ∈ t, ∑ x ∈ s with f x = a, ν x := by
+        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+        intro a ha
+        rw [hfiber a ha μ, hfiber a ha ν, h a]
+      _ = ∑ x ∈ s, ν x := hν
+      _ = distribution f ν δ := rfl
+
+private lemma not_injective_not_ic {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {f g : α → ℝ}
+    (h : ¬ Function.Injective (fun x => (f x, g x))) : ¬ IsICPair f g := by
+  classical
+  obtain ⟨x, y, hpair, hxy⟩ := Function.not_injective_iff.mp h
+  have hfx : f x = f y := congrArg Prod.fst hpair
+  have hgx : g x = g y := congrArg Prod.snd hpair
+  intro hic
+  have hprob (z : α) : Probability (Pi.single z (1 : ℝ)) := by
+    have h : Probability (Convexity.StdSimplex.single (R := ℝ) z).weights :=
+      ⟨(Convexity.StdSimplex.single (R := ℝ) z).weights_nonneg,
+        (Convexity.StdSimplex.single (R := ℝ) z).total_of_fintype⟩
+    simpa only [Convexity.StdSimplex.weights_single, Finsupp.single_eq_pi_single] using h
+  have hf : distribution f (Pi.single x (1 : ℝ)) =
+      distribution f (Pi.single y (1 : ℝ)) := by
+    funext δ
+    unfold distribution
+    simp [hfx]
+  have hg : distribution g (Pi.single x (1 : ℝ)) =
+      distribution g (Pi.single y (1 : ℝ)) := by
+    funext δ
+    unfold distribution
+    simp [hgx]
+  have heq := hic _ _ (hprob x) (hprob y) hf hg
+  have hneq : (Pi.single x (1 : ℝ) : α → ℝ) ≠ Pi.single y (1 : ℝ) := by
+    exact (Pi.single_left_injective (one_ne_zero : (1 : ℝ) ≠ 0)).ne hxy
+  exact hneq heq
+
+private lemma walk_weights {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {f g : α → ℝ}
+    (hinj : Function.Injective (fun x => (f x, g x)))
+    {u v : ℝ ⊕ ℝ} (p : (fiberGraph f g).Walk u v) (hp : p.IsTrail) :
+    ∃ w : α → ℝ,
+      (∀ a, (∑ x ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun x => f x = a), w x) =
+        (if u = Sum.inl a then 1 else 0) - (if v = Sum.inl a then 1 else 0)) ∧
+      (∀ b, (∑ x ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun x => g x = b), w x) =
+        (if v = Sum.inr b then 1 else 0) - (if u = Sum.inr b then 1 else 0)) ∧

+  induction p with
+  | nil =>
+    refine ⟨0, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> simp

+    obtain ⟨w, hwf, hwg, hws, hwb⟩ := ih htail
+    have hedge : s(u, v) ∉ p.edges := (SimpleGraph.Walk.isTrail_cons h p).mp hp |>.2
+    rcases u with a | a <;> rcases v with b | b
+    · unfold fiberGraph at h
+      simp at h
+    · obtain ⟨x, hfx, hgx⟩ : ∃ x, f x = a ∧ g x = b := by
+        unfold fiberGraph at h
+        simpa using h
+      have hwx : w x = 0 := (hws x).mpr (by simpa [hfx, hgx] using hedge)

+      · intro c
+        simp only [Pi.add_apply, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
+        rw [hwf]
+        simp [hfx]
+        split_ifs <;> ring1
+      · intro c
+        simp only [Pi.add_apply, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
+        rw [hwg]
+        simp [hgx]
+      · intro y
+        by_cases hy : y = x
+        · subst y
+          simp [hwx, hfx, hgx]
+        · have hne : s(Sum.inl (f y), Sum.inr (g y)) ≠ s(Sum.inl a, Sum.inr b) := by
+            intro he
+            have he' : f y = a ∧ g y = b := by
+              rw [Sym2.eq_iff] at he
+              simpa using he
+            apply hy
+            exact hinj (Prod.ext (he'.1.trans hfx.symm) (he'.2.trans hgx.symm))
+          simpa [hy, hne] using hws y
+      · intro y
+        by_cases hy : y = x
+        · subst y
+          simp [hwx]
+        · simpa [hy] using hwb y
+    · obtain ⟨x, hfx, hgx⟩ : ∃ x, f x = b ∧ g x = a := by
+        unfold fiberGraph at h
+        simpa using h
+      have hwx : w x = 0 := (hws x).mpr (by simpa [hfx, hgx, Sym2.eq_swap] using hedge)
+      refine ⟨Pi.single x (-1) + w, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
+      · intro c
+        simp only [Pi.add_apply, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
+        rw [hwf]
+        simp [hfx]
+        split_ifs <;> ring1
+      · intro c
+        simp only [Pi.add_apply, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
+        rw [hwg]
+        simp [hgx]
+        split_ifs <;> ring1
+      · intro y
+        by_cases hy : y = x
+        · subst y
+          simp [hwx, hfx, hgx, Sym2.eq_swap]
+        · have hne : s(Sum.inl (f y), Sum.inr (g y)) ≠ s(Sum.inr a, Sum.inl b) := by
+            intro he
+            have he' : f y = b ∧ g y = a := by
+              rw [Sym2.eq_iff] at he
+              simpa using he
+            apply hy
+            exact hinj (Prod.ext (he'.1.trans hfx.symm) (he'.2.trans hgx.symm))
+          simpa [hy, hne] using hws y
+      · intro y
+        by_cases hy : y = x
+        · subst y
+          simp [hwx]
+        · simpa [hy] using hwb y
+    · unfold fiberGraph at h
+      simp at h
+
+private lemma zero_fibers_not_ic {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    {f g w : α → ℝ} (hw : w ≠ 0) (hb : ∀ x, |w x| ≤ 1)
+    (hf : ∀ a, (∑ x ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun x => f x = a), w x) = 0)
+    (hg : ∀ b, (∑ x ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun x => g x = b), w x) = 0) :
+    ¬ IsICPair f g := by
+  classical
+  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ : ∃ x, w x ≠ 0 := Function.ne_iff.mp hw
+  have : Nonempty α := ⟨x⟩
+  let n : ℝ := Fintype.card α
+  have hn : 0 < n := by
+    change (0 : ℝ) < (Fintype.card α : ℝ)
+    exact_mod_cast (Fintype.card_pos : 0 < Fintype.card α)
+  have htotal : ∑ x, w x = 0 := by
+    have hmap : ∀ x ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset α), f x ∈ Finset.univ.image f := by
+      intro x hx
+      exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
+    rw [← Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to hmap w]
+    apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
+    intro a ha
+    exact hf a
+  let μ : α → ℝ := fun x => (1 + w x) / n
+  let ν : α → ℝ := fun _ => 1 / n
+  have hμ : Probability μ := by
+    constructor
+    · intro z
+      have hz := (abs_le.mp (hb z)).1
+      exact div_nonneg (by linarith) hn.le
+    · change (∑ z, (1 + w z) / n) = 1
+      rw [← Finset.sum_div, Finset.sum_add_distrib, htotal]
+      simp [n, ne_of_gt hn]
+  have hν : Probability ν := by
+    constructor
+    · intro z
+      exact le_of_lt (div_pos zero_lt_one hn)
+    · change (∑ _ : α, 1 / n) = 1
+      simp [n, ne_of_gt hn]
+  have hfd : distribution f μ = distribution f ν := by
+    apply (distribution_eq_iff_fiber_sums f μ ν).mpr
+    intro a
+    dsimp [μ, ν]
+    rw [← Finset.sum_div, Finset.sum_add_distrib, hf, add_zero]
+    rw [Finset.sum_div]
+  have hgd : distribution g μ = distribution g ν := by
+    apply (distribution_eq_iff_fiber_sums g μ ν).mpr
+    intro b
+    dsimp [μ, ν]
+    rw [← Finset.sum_div, Finset.sum_add_distrib, hg, add_zero]
+    rw [Finset.sum_div]
+  intro hic
+  have heq := congrFun (hic μ ν hμ hν hfd hgd) x
+  have hval : 1 + w x = 1 := (div_left_inj' hn.ne').mp heq
+  exact hx (by linarith)
+
+private lemma cycle_not_ic {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {f g : α → ℝ}
+    (hinj : Function.Injective (fun x => (f x, g x)))
+    (hcycle : ¬ (fiberGraph f g).IsAcyclic) : ¬ IsICPair f g := by
+  classical
+  obtain ⟨u, p, hp⟩ : ∃ u, ∃ p : (fiberGraph f g).Walk u u, p.IsCycle := by
+    unfold SimpleGraph.IsAcyclic at hcycle
+    push Not at hcycle
+    exact hcycle
+  obtain ⟨w, hwf, hwg, hws, hwb⟩ := walk_weights hinj p hp.isTrail
+  have hw : w ≠ 0 := by
+    intro hw
+    obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := p.edges.exists_mem_of_ne_nil (by simpa using hp.not_nil)
+    have hadj := p.edges_subset_edgeSet he
+    induction e using Sym2.inductionOn with
+    | _ a b =>
+      have hadj' := (fiberGraph f g).mem_edgeSet.mp hadj
+      rcases a with a | a <;> rcases b with b | b
+      · unfold fiberGraph at hadj'
+        simp at hadj'
+      · obtain ⟨x, hfx, hgx⟩ : ∃ x, f x = a ∧ g x = b := by
+          unfold fiberGraph at hadj'
+          simpa using hadj'
+        have hn := (hws x).mp (congrFun hw x)
+        exact hn (by simpa [hfx, hgx] using he)
+      · obtain ⟨x, hfx, hgx⟩ : ∃ x, f x = b ∧ g x = a := by
+          unfold fiberGraph at hadj'
+          simpa using hadj'
+        have hn := (hws x).mp (congrFun hw x)
+        exact hn (by simpa [hfx, hgx, Sym2.eq_swap] using he)
+      · unfold fiberGraph at hadj'
+        simp at hadj'
+  apply zero_fibers_not_ic hw hwb
+  · intro a
+    simpa using hwf a
+  · intro b
+    simpa using hwg b
+
+private lemma ic_injective {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {f g : α → ℝ}
+    (hic : IsICPair f g) : Function.Injective (fun x => (f x, g x)) := by
+  by_contra h
+  exact not_injective_not_ic h hic
+
+private lemma ic_acyclic {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {f g : α → ℝ}
+    (hic : IsICPair f g) (hinj : Function.Injective (fun x => (f x, g x))) :
+    (fiberGraph f g).IsAcyclic := by
+  by_contra h
+  exact cycle_not_ic hinj h hic
+
+private lemma injective_acyclic_ic {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {f g : α → ℝ}
+    (hinj : Function.Injective (fun x => (f x, g x)))
+    (hacyc : (fiberGraph f g).IsAcyclic) : IsICPair f g := by
+  intro μ ν hμ hν hfd hgd
+  classical
+  by_contra hneq
+  let w : α → ℝ := μ - ν
+  have hwne : w ≠ 0 := by
+    exact sub_ne_zero.mpr hneq
+  have hsumf (a : ℝ) :
+      ∑ x ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun x => f x = a), w x = 0 := by
+    have heq := (distribution_eq_iff_fiber_sums f μ ν).mp hfd a
+    simp [w, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, heq]
+  have hsumg (b : ℝ) :
+      ∑ x ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun x => g x = b), w x = 0 := by
+    have heq := (distribution_eq_iff_fiber_sums g μ ν).mp hgd b
+    simp [w, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, heq]
+  let H : SimpleGraph (ℝ ⊕ ℝ) := supportGraph f g w
+  have hHsub : H ≤ fiberGraph f g := by
+    intro v z hadj
+    rcases v with a | a <;> rcases z with b | b
+    · dsimp only [H, supportGraph] at hadj
+      simp at hadj
+    · have hs : ∃ y, f y = a ∧ g y = b ∧ w y ≠ 0 := by
+        dsimp only [H, supportGraph] at hadj
+        simpa using hadj
+      have hs' : ∃ y, f y = a ∧ g y = b := by
+        rcases hs with ⟨y, hfy, hgy, hwy⟩
+        exact ⟨y, hfy, hgy⟩
+      unfold fiberGraph
+      simpa only [SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj, Sum.elim_inl, Sum.elim_inr] using
+        (show Sum.inl a ≠ Sum.inr b ∧
+            ((∃ y, f y = a ∧ g y = b) ∨ False) from
+          ⟨Sum.inl_ne_inr, Or.inl hs'⟩)
+    · have hs : ∃ y, f y = b ∧ g y = a ∧ w y ≠ 0 := by
+        dsimp only [H, supportGraph] at hadj
+        simpa using hadj
+      have hs' : ∃ y, f y = b ∧ g y = a := by
+        rcases hs with ⟨y, hfy, hgy, hwy⟩
+        exact ⟨y, hfy, hgy⟩
+      unfold fiberGraph
+      simpa only [SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj, Sum.elim_inl, Sum.elim_inr] using
+        (show Sum.inr a ≠ Sum.inl b ∧
+            (False ∨ (∃ y, f y = b ∧ g y = a)) from
+          ⟨Sum.inr_ne_inl, Or.inr hs'⟩)
+    · dsimp only [H, supportGraph] at hadj
+      simp at hadj
+  have hHacyc : H.IsAcyclic := hacyc.anti hHsub
+  have hfinite : H.edgeSet.Finite := supportGraph_edge_finite f g w
+  let : Finite H.edgeSet := hfinite.fintype.finite
+  let : H.LocallyFinite := locallyFinite_of_finite_edgeSet H
+  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ : ∃ x, w x ≠ 0 := Function.ne_iff.mp hwne
+  have hxe : H.Adj (Sum.inl (f x)) (Sum.inr (g x)) := by
+    dsimp only [H, supportGraph]
+    rw [SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj]
+    exact ⟨Sum.inl_ne_inr, Or.inl ⟨x, rfl, rfl, hx⟩⟩
+  let C := H.connectedComponentMk (Sum.inl (f x))
+  have hleft : Sum.inl (f x) ∈ C :=
+    SimpleGraph.ConnectedComponent.connectedComponentMk_mem

+title: "Finite-Dimensional Convex Effect Algebras"

+claim: "For random variables f, g on a finite set X and probability measures on X, the pair {f, g} is informationally complete (IC) if equal distributions of f and of g force equal measures. Strongly complementary pairs are IC and IC pairs are complementary; a complementary pair need not be IC, and finding a simple characterization of IC pairs is stated as an open problem."
+strata_touched:

+
+# Gudder, Finite-Dimensional Convex Effect Algebras
+
+S. Gudder, arXiv:1912.05110v1 [quant-ph] (11 December 2019). Quotations are from the v1 TeX source, with the source's macros `\pscript`, `\rscript` and `\brac` expanded.
+
+Section 5 reduces sharp convex effect algebras to classical probability on $X=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$: with $\mathcal P(X)$ the probability measures and $\mathcal R(X)$ the random variables $f\colon X\to\mathbb R$, the distribution of $f$ in $\mu$ is
+
+> $$\Phi_{f,\mu}(\Delta)=\mu[f^{-1}(\Delta)]=\sum\{\mu_i\colon f(i)\in\Delta\}$$
+
+for $\Delta\subseteq\mathbb R$, and
+
+> A set of two random variables $\{f,g\}$ is IC if $\Phi_{f,\mu}=\Phi_{f,\nu}$ and $\Phi_{g,\mu}=\Phi_{g,\nu}$ imply that $\mu=\nu$.
+
+The partition $P(f)$ of $X$ into level sets defines complementary pairs (every nonempty intersection of blocks of $P(f)$ and $P(g)$ is a singleton) and strongly complementary pairs. Theorem 5.2 proves that strongly complementary pairs are IC and that IC pairs are complementary; Example 5 gives a complementary pair, with $P(f)=\{\{1,2\},\{3,4\}\}$ and $P(g)=\{\{1,3\},\{2,4\}\}$, that is not IC. The section ends:
+
+> We conclude from Example 5 that complementarity is a necessary but not a sufficient condition for IC. It is an open problem to find a simple characterization of IC for a pair $\{f,g\}\subseteq\mathcal R(X)$.
+
